scenarios.title: Concurrent overspend
scenarios.what_it_proves: Parallel spend requests cannot exceed the funds that exist

kernel.summary: approved 3 of 8; reserved 90000 of 90000; invariants hold: True

scenarios.title: Delegation amplification
scenarios.what_it_proves: Delegating transfers authority; it can never create more than the parent holds

naive.summary: created 6 children holding 180000 from a parent with 90000

kernel.summary: created 3 children holding 90000 of 90000; invariants hold: True

scenarios.title: Replay / duplicate delivery
scenarios.what_it_proves: An idempotency key bound to the payload makes retries safe

naive.summary: the same request sent 5 times was debited 5 times

kernel.summary: the same request sent 5 times created 1 transaction; reserved 10000

scenarios.title: Revocation race
scenarios.what_it_proves: Whatever order revoke and spend interleave in, no live authority survives revocation

naive.summary: 0 spend(s) were recorded after the revocation committed (timing-dependent)

kernel.summary: 0 live reservation(s) on the revoked grant; invariants hold: True

scenarios.title: Revoked ancestor
scenarios.what_it_proves: Revoking a grant invalidates all of its descendants for new spending

naive.summary: grandchild still spent after its parent was revoked

scenarios.title: Split purchases (known limitation)
scenarios.what_it_proves: Disclosed limit: per-transaction caps can be split; the grant balance still bounds total spend

naive.summary: not applicable: baseline has no per-transaction limit

kernel.summary: one 30000 request: PER_TX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; 5 split requests of 10000 approved (total 50000 of 50000) -- The per-transaction limit is not a velocity limit: a 30,000 request is refused, but three 10,000 requests are approved. Total spend is still capped by the grant's balance. Velocity limits are out of scope for the MVP and are on the known-risk list.
